stats.label: Dr. Diamond’s Metacine has been making significant traction in the space through the strong reputation of its founder, thoughtful, design-forward branding, and a rigorous, results-first approach to skincare. But EyeLift represented a new territory: the brand’s first foray into the eye space, and its most ambitious DTC launch to date.

Fragrance is one of the most difficult categories to sell online - scent can’t be experienced through a screen. For Bistro Waters, D.S. & Durga needed to create desire through visuals, language, and feeling alone.

Derm-led skincare has become one of the most competitive spaces in prestige beauty, crowded with socially-native brands backed by significant budgets. Lancer Skincare had a strong reputation and powerful retail partners - but growing DTC required expanding the narrative beyond Dr. Lancer alone, without diluting the brand’s clinical integrity or luxury positioning.

Lancer Skincare was founded by celebrity dermatologist Dr. Harold Lancer, whose A-list clientele includes Kim Kardashian, Jennifer Lopez, and Victoria Beckham. As part of OGAKI’s ongoing work with the brand, we were challenged with marketing Lancer Skincare’s most luxurious skincare line, the Legacy Collection, which had launched a few years prior and needed more awareness in the market. With a $1,000, 1.7-ounce hero product — The Legacy Youth Treatment — it was no easy feat to spark interest and demand in a product with a super-premium price point. We needed to convince skeptical consumers that this product was worth the price — without the benefit of a “new launch” press hook.

Laura Mercier didn’t need awareness - they needed renewed desire in a culture where makeup moves fast and relevance drives demand. After updating the brand’s creative direction, the risk was clear: if social didn’t reflect the shift immediately and consistently, the refresh wouldn’t land.

Luna Daily, founded by beauty industry veteran Katy Cottam, is a microbiome-balancing body care brand for all skin — even your most intimate. After building momentum in the UK for three years, the brand wanted to expand into the US, but would need to reach an entirely new market of consumers unfamiliar with Luna Daily. With an exclusive US retail partnership with Sephora, Luna Daily had only one chance to make a splashy US launch — and showcase strong initial sales to their retail partner.

Influencer Teni Panosian was launching a brand new skincare line, Monday Born, developed in collaboration with her community. She worked with her audience for testing and feedback to refine each clean, cruelty-free, and vegan product, creating a line that was truly meant for them. The launch posed a unique challenge — we needed to not only educate consumers that the brand existed but quickly and easily explain the innovative new concept of a community-led brand. And though Teni was a well-known beauty creator, she needed help building her credibility as an entrepreneur and founder in a market that often questioned the validity of an influencer-founded brand.

NUFACE is a longstanding pioneer in the at-home microcurrent category, and the only aesthetician-developed, FDA-cleared, and clinically proven technology on the market. But NUFACE was finding itself facing an increasingly crowded market of challengers with aggressive social strategies and creator-first playbooks.

Aire IQ - an intelligent hair dryer - entered a saturated hair tools category where social-first brands were winning attention through narrative as much as innovation. Even with a breakthrough product, a traditional launch risked getting lost in the noise.
